findings.claim: The new checker imports './native-api-manifest.mjs', but no hunk in this diff creates that module, so docs:native-api:check and the site-contract test (which reads the same file) will fail if it is not already committed.
findings.evidence: check-native-api.mjs: `import {verifyNativeApiManifest} from './native-api-manifest.mjs';`; website/tests/site-contract.test.mjs adds `readFile(new URL('../scripts/native-api-manifest.mjs', ...))` and asserts it contains the NEW concept `artifactAggregateSha256` — aggregate-hash manifests are introduced by this change, so the module cannot be pre-existing; yet the diff contains no `website/scripts/native-api-manifest.mjs` hunk and the file tree does not enumerate website/scripts children.
findings.suggested_fix: Include website/scripts/native-api-manifest.mjs in the change (with verifyNativeApiManifest exporting sourceFiles/artifactFileCount and sha256 aggregation), or cite the prior commit that introduced it.

findings.claim: The packed-API source gate hashes every tracked file under every public package directory and compares it to a manifest that can only be regenerated in the release environment, so any routine PR touching a package source, test, or README will fail the Pages workflow with no in-PR remediation path.
findings.evidence: check-generated-artifacts.mjs: `hashTrackedInputs(repositoryRoot, PUBLIC_PACKAGES.map(({directory}) => directory))` uses `git ls-files` over entire package directories (all tracked files, not just API-affecting sources), then `assertEqual(apiSources.sourceAggregateSha256, apiInventory.sourceAggregateSha256, 'packed API source hash drift')`. The workflow runs `pnpm run docs:artifacts:check` on every Pages build, while RELEASING.md states regeneration must happen in 'the release environment that owns the committed artifacts' and the workflow hunk explicitly removes `pnpm run docs:api` regeneration and its git-diff self-heal.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict hashTrackedInputs to files that actually feed TypeDoc (e.g., entry-point type surfaces via the existing exports ledger), or demote source-hash drift to a warning and gate on artifact hash only; otherwise provide an in-workflow regeneration path.

findings.claim: The workflow removes the Flutter and Rust toolchain installs but still runs `pnpm run build:packages`, which previously executed after those toolchains were present; if any workspace package build (e.g., the Flutter package or the Tauri Rust plugin) invokes dart/cargo, the build now breaks.
findings.evidence: Workflow hunk deletes the subosito/flutter-action step and `rustup toolchain install 1.88.0 --profile minimal` yet retains `- name: Build only the npm artifacts needed by snippets / run: pnpm run build:packages`; the file tree shows packages/entity-graph-tauri (whose npm artifact 'bundles the Rust plugin' per native-api.md) and packages/entity_graph_flutter. The postmortem only justifies removing the toolchain for rustdoc, not for package builds.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm and document that build:packages never invokes Flutter/cargo (e.g., via a site-contract assertion on the build script chain), or scope the build to npm-only packages with `pnpm --filter` exclusions.

findings.claim: The committed homepage-mobile-linux.png baseline cannot be validated against the CI rendering environment from this packet, and the postmortem states the canonical Linux baseline still needs to be captured from CI failure evidence — meaning the baseline in this commit may be provisional and the 8% full-page gate can still fail on this PR.
findings.evidence: Postmortem: 'The workflow uploads short-lived Playwright failure evidence so the canonical Linux baseline can be captured without relaxing the comparison' — describing future capture — while the same diff already commits tests/browser/v3-docs-pages.spec.ts-snapshots/homepage-mobile-linux.png (binary, provenance unverifiable). The original failure was a 203px height difference from Linux text wrapping, which is environment-specific.
findings.suggested_fix: Generate the Linux baseline from a CI run of this exact workflow (e.g., via the new artifact upload) before merging, and record that provenance in the postmortem.

findings.claim: The platform branch only special-cases Linux, so developers on Windows fall back to the macOS-tuned homepage-mobile.png baseline and will hit spurious visual failures from platform text wrapping.
findings.evidence: `const mobileSnapshot = process.platform === 'linux' ? 'homepage-mobile-linux.png' : 'homepage-mobile.png';` — any non-Linux, non-macOS platform uses the macOS baseline, the same cross-platform mismatch this change was created to fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Either skip the full-page screenshot assertion off darwin/linux with a logged reason, or key the snapshot name by `${process.platform}` and provide baselines per supported dev platform.
